summary: You choose the Italian Culture, Italian Literature, or Italian and Philosophy subplan. The audit checks the 60 units (66 with Italian and Philosophy), the subplan's courses, WIM and capstone, and electives from 100- and 200-level ITALIAN courses, up to three Italian language courses at or above ITALLANG 21 (12 units) and up to 10 SLE units, with at most 12 units of ITALIAN 199. Every course needs a C or better and a letter grade, except up to 10 PHIL units in the Philosophy subplan. Checked by hand: the OPI, ITALLANG 22A or the equivalent, which courses were taught in Italian, electives from other departments, Bing Overseas Florence, ESF and Digital Humanities, transfer units (up to 12 with approval) and the honors thesis.

So every non-PHIL rule is letter graded. children.name: Philosophy and Literature Capstone Seminar
children.desc: Students must take one course designated as a philosophy and literature capstone. Their choice of capstone seminar must be approved by the Director of Undergraduate Studies (DUS) and the Faculty Advisor for Philosophy.

children.name: Honors Thesis
children.desc:
Students majoring in any DLCL department (i.e., Comparative Literature, French and Italian, German Studies, Iberian and Latin American Cultures, and Slavic Languages and Literatures) who have an overall grade point average (GPA) of 3.3 or above and who maintain a 3.5 (GPA) in their major courses, are eligible to participate in the DLCL’s honors program.
See the Honors webpage for more information.
Program Requirements
To earn honors, students must complete a minimum of 9 units, submit a thesis, and present at the Honors Colloquium at the end of their senior year.

children.name: 5,000-word Topic Paper
children.desc:
The student will write a 5,000-word paper on a topic of their choosing, serving as the culmination of their work in the field.
To write the paper, students must enroll in a 3-unit, letter-grade independent study with a faculty member (or affiliate) in the Philosophy and Literature Focal Group. The paper must involve philosophy and literature, and the faculty member must approve the topic by the add/drop deadline.

add.why: The WIM and capstone sections list one rule per subplan ("Italian Culture & Italian Literature Writing in the Major", "Italian and Philosophy Writing in the Major", "Italian Culture Capstone Experience", "Italian Literature Capstone Experience", "Italian and Philosophy Capstone Experience"); each moves into its subplan so a student is held only to their own. Options: a capstone seminar "approved by the Director of Undergraduate Studies (DUS) and the Faculty Advisor for Philosophy"; the DLCL honors thesis ("a minimum of 9 units, submit a thesis"); or the topic paper written in "a 3-unit, letter-grade independent study".
"To earn honors, students must complete a minimum of 9 units, submit a thesis, and present at the Honors Colloquium at the end of their senior year."
Other requirements: "Gateway course; ITALLANG22A or equiv.; Oral Proficiency Interview (OPI)". Equivalents (placement, other second-year courses) need a judgment.
